chapter_title: Concerning the Interpretation of the Fourteen [Gre
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

---

**¶3:** Know this: that the [GAP-1] spiritual faculties in the lower degrees of the mind dwell within fourteen [GAP-2: complete states of interior life]: the five essential capacities of spiritual perception — the goods and truths derived from the Primordial Divine Human — together with the Divine Influx and its Reception. These consecrate those faculties with divine good, dwelling within them interiorly. They constitute a sevenfold fullness: five capacities of perception united with the twofold operation of revelation and understanding.

---

**¶4:** [GAP-3: And the] five powers of sustaining good proceeding from the Active Divine [GAP-4: REVIEW uphold] the entire burden of the spiritual order from highest to lowest; together with the Active Divine Proceeding and the Primordial Divine Human, from whom these powers originate. These are the fourteen acknowledgments of the Divine that have been proclaimed — the worship constituted of fourteen conjunctions with the Divine — by which the whole spiritual order is sustained and given form.

---

**¶5:** There are fourteen complete states of wisdom [GAP-5] belonging to the interior spiritual principle [GAP-6: REVIEW] [GAP-7] concerning them in his conjunction with the Divine, for they are made manifest [GAP-8: within the interior ground of good] that has not yet been disclosed to external awareness. This interior ground [GAP-9: of good is made firm and] established. These powers endured against the assault of falsity from evil [GAP-10: and nothing] equals them. The hidden fullness of divine good that [GAP-11] — the Divine Truth Proceeding who came forth from the Divine Love, the [GAP-12] — He came and stood immovable in the center of these [GAP-13: spiritual states]: he is called the benevolent originating good of [GAP-14: REVIEW all] the states of wisdom and divine powers that are sanctified and conjoined in unity. He has become the sovereign ruling principle and supreme governing authority according to the very form of the Originating Divine Love, the lord over all these providential purposes. The entire spiritual order coheres through their united divine intention [GAP-15] unto the final fulfillment of all ends.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: Happen you know this, that the [powers] below abide in fourteen [great aeons of life]: the five elements, the sons of the First Man, together with the Call and the Hearing. They anoint them, living in them. These shall make seven, five plus two.

[And the] f[ive s]ons of the Living Spirit who [support] all [the wei]ght of the universe; together with the [Li]vi[ng] Spirit [and the Fir]st Man, their fathers. These are the fourt[een p]raises that he has proclaimed, the praise that is made of fourteen pra[yers], by which the universe is established.

[There are fourt]een aeons of light [in the land] of Seth [he] [spoke] about them in his prayer, for they are expl[ai]ned [in the la]nd that is not revealed. This land [of life is made firm and estab]lished. They bore up under the Enemy [and nothing equa]ls them. The hidden plenitude that [is in] the Ambassador who came from the Father, the [most high] He came and stood firm in the midst of these [aeons]: he is called the good father of [all] the ae[ons and gods] who are holy and conjoined. He has become leader and a great king after the likeness of the first Father, the lord of all these cou[nse]ls. This universe is held together by their will [from the beginning] to the end of all things.

fills.explanation: The spiritual reading says "spiritual faculties in the lower degrees," and in the Kephalaia's natural-plane register, "powers" is the standard term for divine spiritual faculties or capacities that dwell within the aeons.

The spiritual reading specifies "complete states of interior life"; "great aeons" is partially visible and "of life" translates "of interior life" into the Kephalaia's cosmological register, where life corresponds to divine good indwelling.

The spiritual reading confirms "And the" as the connector linking the second group of seven (¶4) to the first group (¶3), introducing the five sons of the Living Spirit as the complementary sustaining powers.

The editor's "support" correctly renders the natural-plane action of the five sons of the Living Spirit bearing the weight of the cosmos; the spiritual reading's "uphold" confirms the same function, and "support" is the appropriate physical-plane Manichaean term.

The spiritual reading says "belonging to the interior spiritual principle"; in the Kephalaia register "in the land of Seth" expresses this belonging, and "the land" directly connects to the twice-mentioned "land" in the sentences that follow.

The editor's "e" reflects the visible Coptic pronominal prefix (ⲉϥ-); in English translation this should be rendered as the pronoun "he," referring back to Seth as the subject who spoke about the aeons in prayer.

The spiritual reading indicates Seth communicated "concerning them in his conjunction with the Divine"; "spoke" is the natural-plane verb for this act, yielding the grammatical clause "he spoke about them in his prayer."

The spiritual reading says "within the interior ground of good"; in the Kephalaia register "in the land" is the natural-plane equivalent, and the fill "in the la" + visible "nd" completes to "in the land that is not revealed."

fills.fill: of life is made firm and estab
fills.explanation: The spiritual reading gives "of good is made firm and established"; in the Kephalaia "of life" renders "of good" (life = divine good in correspondence), and "is made firm and estab[lished]" completes the visible ending, strongly constrained by the visible text and parallel phrasing.

The spiritual reading gives "and nothing equals them"; "and nothing equa" + visible "ls" completes to "and nothing equals them," expressing that no opposing force matches these sustaining powers — strongly constrained by the visible ending.

The spiritual reading identifies the hidden fullness of divine good as indwelling within the Divine Truth Proceeding (Ambassador); "is in" expresses the Swedenborgian principle that divine good (plenitude) is the esse within divine truth, yielding "the hidden plenitude that is in the Ambassador."

The spiritual reading identifies this as a title for the Divine Love (the Father); "most high" is a well-attested Manichaean epithet for the Father of Greatness and corresponds to Swedenborg's Altissimus — the inmost Divine — fitting the appositional title pattern used throughout this passage.

The spiritual reading says "spiritual states," and throughout this chapter the fourteen spiritual states are consistently called "aeons" in the natural-plane register; "he stood firm in the midst of these aeons" parallels the chapter's recurring framework.

The editor's "all" is confirmed by the spiritual reading ("the benevolent originating good of all the states of wisdom"); "all" expresses the universality of the Ambassador's paternal governance over every aeon and god.

The spiritual reading says "unto the final fulfillment of all ends," and the gap precedes "to the end of all things"; "from the beginning" creates the standard Manichaean temporal inclusio "from the beginning to the end," expressing the complete span of providential governance.
